subject: Trident Health: ephemeral debug logs retention and SIG/CAIQ evidence
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@tridenthealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Trident Legal <contracts@tridenthealth.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Short-term debug logs / evidence for SIG/CAIQ

Hi Naomi,

Quick follow-up from our security review: our SecurityOps team is asking whether Trident can get a short-term extension of debug/log retention for a subset of tenants (specifically for incident forensics and regulatory investigations). Our default is 30 days, but regulators here sometimes require 90 days of trace for a very small number of mattered tenants — we only need "on-demand" extensions tied to a retained evidence packet.

Two asks from our side:
- Can Redwood create tenant-scoped exceptions for ephemeral debug logs and, if so, what controls are applied to limit scope and access?
- Can you provide an evidence packet that maps to SIG/CAIQ questions around data deletion proof, segregated logs, and proof-of-delete for such exceptions (customer-specific attestation preferred)?

We know this is sensitive; happy to sign an addendum if necessary. Also note our contracts team (cc'd) will want to see the proposed gating and an administration audit trail.

Thanks — can you loop in whoever owns log retention and compliance artifacts?

— Alex
Alex Turner
Director, Security Operations
Trident Health
attachment: trident_initial_scope.csv (xlsx stub)
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@tridenthealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Short-term debug logs / evidence for SIG/CAIQ

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear note.

Short answer: yes, we support tenant-scoped temporary retention extensions for debug/session logs, but they are tightly gated. High-level controls we apply:
- Per-tenant retention flags implemented at the routing layer (only affects debug/session artifacts, not core production data).
- Access restricted to a named SRE/Compliance RBAC group; all access is audited with immutable audit records.
- Extensions are timeboxed (e.g., 30/60/90 days) and require an admin request plus a signed addendum for anything >30 days.
- Proof-of-delete: we can provide a deletion manifest and Signed SHA-256 manifests for sanitized exports and a timestamped deletion job log.

I'm looping in Jordan and Irene to pull together the SIG/CAIQ-aligned evidence packet and a proposed temporary-retention addendum. Jordan/Irene — can you confirm which artifacts we can deliver by COB Monday and what needs legal review?

Regards,
Naomi Feldman
Director, Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Naomi/Irene — quick internal note and proposed deliverables.

We can assemble the following artifacts without involving Legal for the first pass:
1) Redacted evidence packet (PDF) that maps Redwood control IDs to SIG/CAIQ questions covering deletion, retention flags, and admin audit trails. (will export as redwood_sig_caiq_evidence_packet_v1.pdf)
2) Tenant-scoped retention matrix (Excel) showing which log types are eligible for extension, TTL defaults, and maximum allowable extension windows (will be the attached trident_log_scope_matrix.xlsx).
3) Procedure doc and deletion manifest template (docx) that Trident can use to request an extension and to accept proof-of-delete artifacts. (temporary-retention-addendum-draft.docx)
4) Example signed deletion manifest (SHA256 checksums + job run timestamps) — we will sanitize tenant identifiers for pre-release.

Controls notes:
- Admin approval flow: extension requests must be approved by 2 people (SRE manager + Trust lead) and are recorded in our audit ledger (immutable).
- Access to extended logs uses short-lived credentials with MFA enforced.
- We can provide event-level access logs for any accesses to extended retention buckets.

ETA: I can produce items (1)-(3) and the example manifest by EOD Monday (2026-11-30). Legal will need to review the addendum for anything that changes contractual data handling >30 days; I'll flag that doc.

Subject: Re: Short-term debug logs / evidence for SIG/CAIQ — proposed artifacts and next steps

Alex — thanks for the patience. We pulled together the artifacts Jordan outlined and attached the initial packet for your review. Summary and next steps below.

What we attached:
- redwood_sig_caiq_evidence_packet_v1.pdf — maps Redwood controls to SIG/CAIQ sections covering deletion, retention flags, proof-of-delete artifacts, and admin audit trails.
- trident_log_scope_matrix.xlsx — tenant-scoped matrix: log classes, default TTL, allowed extension windows, minimum justification fields.
- temporary-retention-addendum-draft.docx — draft addendum your contracts team can review with sample gating language and approval flow.

Key constraints we enforce:
- Extensions are tenant-scoped, timeboxed, and must include a documented justification.
- Audit trail: all extension requests and accesses appear in our immutable audit ledger (we provide export for up to 2 years) and are included in the evidence packet.
- Proof-of-delete: upon expiry we run a deletion job and provide a signed manifest (SHA-256) and a job log with start/finish timestamps.

Next actions we recommend:
1) Trident Legal to review the addendum and propose any language edits (I left placeholders for SLAs/penalties). DocuSign link is included if you want to sign a short-term pilot addendum: https://app.docusign.com/prepare/Trident-Temporary-Retention-Addendum
2) If accepted, provide the tenant list (sample CSV) and the desired retention windows per tenant. We will schedule a short (30-min) kickoff with our SREs to confirm access controls and who will appear in the approval workflow.
3) We will deliver the signed deletion manifest example and full packet exports within the pilot window.

Attachments (sent): redwood_sig_caiq_evidence_packet_v1.pdf, trident_log_scope_matrix.xlsx, temporary-retention-addendum-draft.docx

If you want, we can redact the evidence packet further before Legal review. Let me know the timeline your team prefers.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
